question: Can the 2013 Lingayen Gulf reforested-mangrove fish study be used as regional fish evidence when one institutional record marks it withdrawn and the available copies contain only abstracts?

method.summary: Compared the UPLB Knowledge Repository records 4086 and 5775 with the Ateneo Archium record for the same title and authors. Reviewed only institutional bibliographic pages and abstracts; all three pages say the document/full text is unavailable. No journal PDF, tables, fish names, data, correction, retraction notice, or reason for withdrawal was retrieved.
method.withdrawalFinding: UPLB record 4086 explicitly states 'This paper has been withdrawn.' UPLB record 5775 and the Ateneo institutional record retain the same article abstract and citation but do not display that withdrawal notice. The reason, date, responsible publisher decision, and whether a corrected replacement exists were not established. Treat this as an unresolved publication-status conflict and hold the work from species evidence.
method.abstractOnlyLead: The institutional abstracts describe five planted-mangrove stands in Anda, Alaminos, Bolinao, and Bani, sampled in December 2008 and February 2009 with a modified triangular trap near the plantation edge at low tide. They report 593 individuals and 50 species from 22 families. These are abstract-reported claims from a work flagged withdrawn, not accepted survey results or validated fish records.
method.localityAndHabitatLimit: The abstract's five site labels are Tondol (Anda), Pangapisan (Alaminos), Imbo (Anda), Pilar (Bolinao), and Bangrin (Bani), Pangasinan. It describes planted mangrove stands in northwestern Lingayen Gulf. No coordinates, exact waterbody/reach boundaries, site-to-species matrix, or geometry are available in the reviewed records.
method.reuseFinding: The institutional records expose no full text or item-specific reuse license. No species table, article content beyond short citation/abstract metadata, figure, photo, or dataset was copied or redistributed.

studyAreaLead.sourceNameAsReported: Planted mangrove stands in northwestern Lingayen Gulf
studyAreaLead.habitatLane: mangrove intertidal/coastal transition; site-level salinity and aquatic-body linkage unresolved

publication.title: Evaluating patterns of fish assemblage changes from different-aged reforested mangroves in Lingayen Gulf
publication.citation: Peralta-Milan, S. A., & Salmo III, S. G. (2013). Evaluating patterns of fish assemblage changes from different-aged reforested mangroves in Lingayen Gulf. Journal of Environmental Science and Management, 16(1), 11–19.
publication.fullTextStatus: Unavailable from the reviewed UPLB and Ateneo records.
publication.withdrawalReason: Not stated on the reviewed record.

interpretation: The withdrawal notice takes precedence for evidence handling until an authoritative journal correction, replacement, or explanation resolves the conflicting institutional records. Do not cite its abstract totals as accepted fish-survey results.

Because the full article is unavailable, the abstract cannot establish species identities, station-specific catch, sampling effort details beyond the abstract wording, vouchers, or the reason the work was withdrawn.
The site names remain discovery leads only; no mangrove polygon, estuary boundary, salinity class, fishing access, current presence, safety, diet, legal status, or conservation claim is inferred.
No species assertions, occurrence rows, counts used as accepted evidence, waterbody assignments, coordinates, geometry, photos, or public app content were added. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.

decision.reason: An official UPLB repository item explicitly marks the paper withdrawn; duplicate institutional records omit the notice, but full text and a primary explanation are unavailable.

nextAction: Look for an authoritative journal withdrawal/correction notice or a clearly identified replacement version with full methods, species tables, sample provenance, and item-specific reuse terms. Until resolved, exclude this study from fish evidence and continue searching independent Pangasinan mangrove, estuary, and inland-water sources.
